title: Death's End
author: Liu, Cixin
review:
I made this review very non-spoiler for those interested in the series as a whole.

This is definitely one of my favorite sci-fi books and series, Liu has a huge amount of really cool and often crazy ideas packed into this one. He could have gone the easy path for this final book but he went down the more interesting path and the story goes in directions you wouldn't expect after the end of book 2. This book is incredibly heavy and dark at times, I loved it but it took some time to chew on the ideas and the implications of the plot developments. There's a healthy dose of nihilism in this book, but often sci-fi is a bit too optimistic for my tastes and this has a good kick in the teeth for overly optimistic sci-fi. You could probably label parts as grimdark sci-fi as there's some definite bleak moments that are intense and graphic as well as existentially disturbing.

I'll be thinking about this series for quite some time, I absolutely loved my time with it and this is the reason I read sci-fi in general. I can see why this wouldn't be for everyone but personally this is right up my alley. Will be interested in anything Liu comes out with in the future.
